'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|50%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Janet Mills]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Janet Mills]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsME}} The '''2022 Maine gubernatorial election''' took place on November 8, 2022, to elect the [[governor of Maine]]. Incumbent [[Maine Democratic Party|Democratic]] governor [[Janet Mills]] won re-election to a second term, defeating [[Maine Republican Party|Republican]] nominee and former governor [[Paul LePage]]. Neither candidate faced any [[Partisan primary|primary]] opposition.{{Cite web |date=2022-06-14 |title=Republican Paul LePage looks ahead to Main's November governor race against Gov. Janet Mills |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/republican-paul-lepage-looks-ahead-to-mains-november-governor-race-against-gov-janet-mills |access-date=2022-06-15 |website=PBS NewsHour |language=en-us}}{{cite web|url=https://www.wmtw.com/article/its-official-janet-mills-versus-paul-lepage-in-maine-gubernatorial-race-this-november/39457571#|title=It's official: Janet Mills versus Paul LePage in Maine gubernatorial race this November|author=Hirschkorn, Phil|date=March 16, 2022|work=WMTW}} An independent candidate, Sam Hunkler, received 2% of the vote, the lowest total for a third party or independent gubernatorial candidate in the state since [[1982 Maine gubernatorial election|1982]]. This was the first gubernatorial election in Maine since [[1990 Maine gubernatorial election|1990]] in which the winner was from the same party as the [[Joe Biden|incumbent president]], and the first time since [[1978 Maine gubernatorial election|1978]] that it was a Democrat. With nearly 377,000 votes, Mills won more votes than any other gubernatorial candidate in Maine history, breaking her own record set [[2018 Maine gubernatorial election|four years earlier]]. Her 13-point margin of victory was the largest for a statewide Democratic candidate since [[George J. Mitchell]] won over 80% of the vote in the [[1988 United States Senate election in Maine|1988 United States Senate election]]. However, Maine had not elected a governor from the same party as the President since [[1990 Maine gubernatorial election|1990]], and some Democrats were afraid that Democratic president [[Joe Biden]]'s low approval ratings would hurt Mills.{{Cite web |last1=Strimling |first1=Ethan |last2=Harriman |first2=Phil |date=2022-04-21 |title=Opinion: A red wave may be coming to Maine |url=http://www.bangordailynews.com/2022/04/21/opinion/opinion-contributor/a-red-wave-may-be-coming-to-maine-joam40zk0w/ |access-date=2023-02-06 |website=Bangor Daily News |language=en-US}} Access to [[abortion]] became a crucial issue following the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]]'s ruling in ''[[Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization]]'', which overturned ''[[Roe v. Wade]]'' and eliminated the constitutional right to abortion, effectively returning the issue to the states. Following the leak of the draft opinion, Mills released a statement saying "I do not consider the rights of women to be dispensable. And I pledge that as long as I am governor, I will fight with everything I have to protect reproductive rights and to preserve access to reproductive health care in the face of every and any threat to it – whether from politicians in [[Augusta, Maine|Augusta]] or Supreme Court Justices in Washington."{{Cite web |last=Billings |first=Randy |date=2022-05-03 |title=Gov. Mills pledges to protect abortion access; LePage emphasizes his support of restrictions |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2022/05/03/gov-mills-pledges-to-fight-to-protect-reproductive-rights/ |access-date=2023-02-06 |website=Press Herald}} After the release of the draft opinion, LePage stated he supported some abortion restrictions, but pledged to preserve access to abortion in cases of rape, incest and life of the mother. However, this was seen as a reversal over his previous statements, including one in 2016 where he said that "we should not have abortion,"{{Cite web |last=Jason |first=PAFUNDI |date=2016-01-16 |title=Abortion opponents rally in Augusta |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2016/01/16/abortion-opponents-rally-in-augusta/ |access-date=2023-02-06 |website=Press Herald}} and a 2018 statement in support of overturning ''Roe v. Wade.''{{Cite news |last=Wong |first=Amy B |date=October 5, 2022 |title=Maine GOP gubernatorial hopeful struggles with abortion questions in debate |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2022/10/05/maine-governor-lepage-mills-abortion/ |newspaper=The Washington Post}} LePage would continue to struggle with questions on abortion, and a stumble in a debate with Mills on the topic led to national headlines.{{Cite news |last1=McFadden |first1=Alyce |last2=Bender |first2=Michael C. |date=2022-10-05 |title=LePage Stumbles on Abortion Questioning in Maine Governor's Debate |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/10/04/us/politics/lepage-mills-abortion-maine-debate.html |access-date=2023-02-06 |issn=0362-4331}} Over the course of the campaign, Mills developed a fundraising advantage over LePage,{{Cite web |last=Billings |first=Randy |date=2022-09-27 |title=Gov. Mills widens fundraising advantage over LePage |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2022/09/27/mills-grows-fundraising-lead-over-lepage/ |access-date=2023-02-06 |website=Press Herald}} while outside groups unaffiliated with either campaign broke records for spending, mostly on negative ads. Ads supporting Mills's candidacy or opposing LePage's candidacy accounted for over $9 million in spending, while ads supporting LePage or opposing Mills accounted for over $7 million.{{Cite web |last=Randy BillingsStaff Writer |date=2022-10-28 |title=Spending in Maine gubernatorial race surges to new record |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2022/10/28/spending-surges-to-new-record-in-maine-gubernatorial-race/ |access-date=2023-02-06 |website=Press Herald}} Polls released after the primaries showed Mills having a moderate-to-large lead over LePage, with the closest poll showing her ahead by six points. Mills was declared the winner by the Associated Press shortly before midnight on November 8. LePage did not immediately concede the race,{{Cite web |last1=Stein |first1=Adrienne |last2=Bourgault |first2=Matthew |date=2022-11-09 |title=Gov. Mills declares victory, LePage not conceding defeat |url=https://wgme.com/news/local/governor-janet-mills-declares-victory-paul-lepage-not-conceding-defeat-maine-gubernatorial-race |access-date=2023-02-06 |website=WGME |language=en}} but did concede on November 9 with a written statement.{{Cite web |date=2022-11-09 |title=Former Gov. LePage concedes, cites 'grave' concerns over inflation for Maine |url=https://www.wmtw.com/article/former-gov-lepage-concedes-concerns-inflation-maine/41913610 |access-date=2023-02-06 |website=WMTW |language=en}} In his election night remarks, LePage concluded that he "missed the message" on abortion.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=November 9, 2022 |title=Paul LePage says Mainers made the wrong choice following failed bid for Blaine House |url=https://www.wabi.tv/2022/11/09/paul-lepage-says-mainers-made-wrong-choice-following-failed-bid-blaine-house/ |access-date=2023-02-07 |website=WABI-TV |language=en}} Some observers saw the results as symbolic of the decline of the once-dominant [[Maine Republican Party]], and Maine's movement towards becoming a solid [[Red states and blue states|blue state]].{{Cite web |last=Woodard |first=Colin |date=2022-11-13 |title=Midterms reveal Republican decline across large swaths of Maine |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2022/11/13/midterms-reveal-republican-decline-across-large-swaths-of-maine/ |access-date=2023-02-06 |website=Press Herald}} In the election, Mills broke her own record set four years earlier for most votes received by a Maine gubernatorial candidate. ===Predictions=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !
